questions.noidung: Sleep is not simply a time when the brain switches off. During sleep, the brain organises the information it collected during the day and stores important memories. Students who sleep well before an exam usually remember more than those who stay up all night. However, sleeping too little over many weeks can weaken attention and slow down decision-making. Experts therefore recommend a regular bedtime, a dark room and no screens for at least an hour before sleep.

questions.noidung: Every year, millions of tonnes of plastic end up in the ocean. Some of it floats on the surface, but much of it sinks or breaks into tiny pieces called microplastics. Fish often mistake these pieces for food, and the plastic then enters the food chain. Scientists warn that cleaning the ocean alone cannot solve the problem. Reducing single-use plastic and improving waste collection on land are far more effective long-term solutions.
